title: Two Bodies, One Plant Life Cycle

scenes.tts: The green cushion of moss on a shady wall is haploid. Its cells carry one set of chromosomes, the same count as a human egg. In your body, the only cells with one set are made while eggs and sperm form. So where is the diploid moss?
scenes.visual: Moss cushion block beside a human egg chip, both marked one set; a dashed question box for the diploid moss.
scenes.narration: The green cushion of moss on a shady wall is haploid. Its cells carry one set of chromosomes, the same count as a human egg. In your body, the only cells with one set are made while eggs and sperm form. So where is the diploid moss?

scenes.tts: Land plants grow two multicellular bodies in one life cycle. The haploid body is the gametophyte, and the diploid body, with two sets of chromosomes, is the sporophyte. Each body gives rise to the other. Biologists call this alternation of generations. In humans and other mammals, meiosis makes eggs and sperm directly, and there is no haploid body.
scenes.visual: Two body blocks with arrows both ways; then a mammal strip where meiosis goes straight to eggs and sperm and the haploid body slot is empty.
scenes.narration: Land plants grow two multicellular bodies in one life cycle. The haploid body is the gametophyte, and the diploid body, with two sets of chromosomes, is the sporophyte. Each body gives rise to the other. Biologists call this alternation of generations. In humans and other mammals, meiosis makes eggs and sperm directly, and there is no haploid body.

scenes.tts: To read any life cycle, find two events first. Meiosis halves the chromosome number, from diploid to haploid. Fertilization joins egg and sperm, and restores the diploid number. In a basic plant cycle, those are the only two places the number changes, so the stages between them share one label. Mitosis, which copies a cell, never changes it.
scenes.visual: A bare loop; meiosis and fertilization markers appear; the loop splits into a haploid arc and a diploid arc.
scenes.narration: To read any life cycle, find two events first. Meiosis halves the chromosome number, from diploid to haploid. Fertilization joins egg and sperm, and restores the diploid number. In a basic plant cycle, those are the only two places the number changes, so the stages between them share one label. Mitosis, which copies a cell, never changes it.

scenes.tts: In a land plant, cells of the sporophyte undergo meiosis, and the products are spores, not gametes. A spore divides by mitosis into the gametophyte. The gametophyte makes eggs and sperm by mitosis, because its cells are already haploid. Fertilization gives a zygote, the single fertilized cell. The zygote divides by mitosis into a new sporophyte.
scenes.visual: The five stages appear on the loop as a token travels around it, each stage coloured by its arc.
scenes.narration: In a land plant, cells of the sporophyte undergo meiosis, and the products are spores, not gametes. A spore divides by mitosis into the gametophyte. The gametophyte makes eggs and sperm by mitosis, because its cells are already haploid. Fertilization gives a zygote, the single fertilized cell. The zygote divides by mitosis into a new sporophyte.

scenes.tts: In a moss, the leafy green shoot is the gametophyte, and the sporophyte is a thin stalk with a capsule. In a fern, the frond is the sporophyte, and the gametophyte is a small prothallus that lives on its own. In a pine, the tree is the sporophyte, and the male gametophyte is a pollen grain. In the flowering plant Arabidopsis, the green plant is the sporophyte. The gametophytes are the pollen grain and the embryo sac.
scenes.visual: Four columns, each with a sporophyte block and a gametophyte block; which one is large changes from moss to fern, pine and Arabidopsis.

In a fern, the frond is the sporophyte, and the gametophyte is a small prothallus that lives on its own. In a pine, the tree is the sporophyte, and the male gametophyte is a pollen grain. In the flowering plant Arabidopsis, the green plant is the sporophyte. The gametophytes are the pollen grain and the embryo sac.

scenes.tts: So the diploid moss was there all along. It is the stalk and capsule that grow from the zygote. The big body is the haploid gametophyte in a moss, but the diploid sporophyte in a fern, a pine and a flowering plant. So do not guess from size. Find meiosis and fertilization first, then label every stage.
